---
title: "Why follow through?"
subtitle: "We voted. The work isn't finished."
---

It's easy to treat civic life as something we do on Election Day: show up, fill in the bubbles, and go home. Baltimore Ballot starts with a different idea. Our vote is one part of a decision, not the last thing we can do about it.

This project starts with friends trying to understand what we were asked to decide. What did a question actually mean? What did we authorize? What happens after the result—and where can we still have a say?

We start with ballot measures and follow the questions they raise about Baltimore's money, services, and government. The goal is to connect understanding a decision with taking part in what comes next.

## Who is “we”?

“We” means us as neighbors and voters, not a newsroom or a group that agrees on everything. Everett Anderson makes and maintains this site. The invitation is shared: let's understand these decisions and follow them through together.

## How we keep this useful {#editorial-standards}

We link to the records behind the explanations, distinguish what we know from what still needs checking, and explain important limitations beside the work. Results are labeled certified only when verified against a source. When a substantive factual mistake is corrected, the affected page will say what changed and when.

The guides explain the choices without telling anyone how to vote. Where we identify a way to participate, we'll connect it to a specific decision or next step rather than offer a vague instruction to get involved.

Baltimore Ballot is independent of city government and political campaigns.
